# dreamrouter_host (Resource)

A device with a fixed IP address and a DNS name. The router serves the name like an A record, but stores it on the device, and only while the device has a fixed IP, so both are managed together.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A device with a fixed IP and a DNS name, managed together.
resource "dreamrouter_host" "nas" {
  name = "nas.home.internal"
  ip   = "192.168.1.50"
  mac  = "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01"
}

# Other records can point at it.
resource "dreamrouter_dns_record" "files" {
  type  = "CNAME"
  name  = "files.home.internal"
  value = dreamrouter_host.nas.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip` (String) The fixed IPv4 address. It must be in one of the router's networks, and not reserved for another device.
- `mac` (String) The device's MAC address, in lower-case colon form (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff). Changing it replaces the host.
- `name` (String) The device's DNS name, e.g. "nas.home.internal". It can't also be a static DNS record or another device's name. Changing it renames the host in place.

### Optional

- `device_name` (String) The device name shown in the web UI. If not set, a device the router already knows keeps its name, and a new device is labelled with the host name.
- `forget_on_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, remove the device from the router entirely (its name and history), instead of only removing its fixed IP and DNS name. Defaults to false.
- `network_id` (String) ID of the network the IP belongs to (see the dreamrouter_networks data source). Defaults to the network whose subnet contains ip.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The device's client ID on the router.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = dreamrouter_host.nas
  id = "nas.home.internal"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by host name (or the device's MAC address):
terraform import dreamrouter_host.nas nas.home.internal
```
